subject: Re: Encord & Rise Up Labs - POC thread
text:
*Hi Winnie,*

I hope you've been doing well.

I wanted to reach out and reconnect regarding the opportunity to work
together again.

First, I'd like to acknowledge that our last engagement did not meet
the standard
that either of us expected. We take full responsibility for that outcome,
and we've spent time reflecting on what went wrong and, more importantly,
how to improve.

Since then, we've significantly strengthened our approach to AI data
operations. We've built a more experienced annotation team, introduced
tighter screening and QA processes, improved project supervision, and
established a much stronger operational framework to ensure consistent
quality and delivery.

With these improvements in place, I wanted to ask if you'd be open to
giving us another opportunity, starting with a *very small POC*. We believe
this is the best way to demonstrate the progress we've made and rebuild
your confidence in our capabilities without requiring a significant
commitment from your side.

If the POC meets your expectations, we'd be delighted to discuss broader
collaboration. If not, you'll have a clear evaluation with minimal risk.

We truly value the opportunity to work with Encord and would appreciate
another chance to prove ourselves.

Looking forward to hearing your thoughts.

subject: Re: Follow Up to our Discussion- Encord
text:
Hi Zachary,

 I gave Claude Code Label Studio's React plugin documentation page and then
told it to create the UI there.
Then it coded out and pushed the changes there. I tested the UI and then
told Claude some bugs and then it fixed directly.
I never looked into the source code directly as the UI will be only facing
annotators and annotators will also report issue to me so all these changes
are very low risk.

It supported drawing table boundary lines pretty easily and I can multi
select the grids to create merge cells easily. I then created Excel like
interaction page pretty easily too where I can copy paste and modify bulk
number of table cells.
Maintenance is pretty easy since I just rely on vibe code and the risk of
breaking is very low.

Beyond parsing UI, we care about for managing different roles for
annotators and controlling their access on data.

Given Label Studio gives full flexibility on code, what matters the most is
if Encord can match this feature.
I can build any UI without needing any front end engineer or ask infra
engineer on deployment which is super handy for MLE to iterate fast and
experiment on different ways of annotating
I can instantly apply changes that annotators flagged.

But something I think Encord could be better is the support and
responsivensss. Given it was really difficult to get Label Studio's
attention, we find that part a risk.

Best,
Joon

subject: Re: AeroVect <> Encord | Post demo follow-up
text:
Hi Zachary,

Thanks for the questions — answers below:

   1. *Derivation method:* Velocity is currently calculated frame-to-frame.
   We take the distance the cuboid moved between two consecutive frames and
   divide by the time elapsed between them.
   2. *Fusion with other signals:* No fusion — velocity is derived purely
   from the annotated cuboid positions over time. No radar, IMU, or wheel
   odometry is involved.
   3. *The spike-flagging script:* Unfortunately we're not able to share
   the scripts themselves, but the logic is the same frame-to-frame approach
   described above: take the cuboid position in two frames, compute the
   distance moved, and divide by the time between the frames.
   4. *The 10–20cm figure:* That's not just illustrative — we do see it in
   practice, though the exact range depends on the application.

Best,
Aadit Patel
Perception Engineer
AeroVect Technologies Inc.
